testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: If driving a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times while operating a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
Protect the driver's head when entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards (also called headache racks) protect the driver from cargo moving forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: For safety, when should you turn off a retarder?

options.text: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
When you are carrying a passenger.
When you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy.
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow a vehicle and reduces braking. However, it can cause wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn off the retarder when conditions are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, you apply the parking brake by:
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix the vehicle.
Formally request that you fix the vehicle's problems.
Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a commercial motor vehicle unsafe, they can take it out of service until it is fixed.

questions.question: If driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used after crossing railroad tracks.
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be turned on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off once your vehicle has completely cleared the tracks.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be strong and secure to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong and secure to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, the header board should be secure, undamaged, and strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is using their high beam headlights, you should:

options.text: Flash your high beams to remind them to switch to low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight a manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh.
The maximum weight a single vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a single vehicle can haul.
The maximum weight that can be loaded onto a single trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight a manufacturer says a loaded vehicle can weigh.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight the manufacturer states a vehicle and its load can weigh.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares, plus a charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: After starting the engine, when should oil pressure reach a normal level?
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, watch the gauges. Oil pressure should rise to normal within a few seconds.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Prevent the front tires from skidding
Prevent the front tires from overheating

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the front tires from skidding
questions.explanation: Older air brake vehicles have front brake limiting valves. These were designed to reduce front wheel skidding. However, research shows they are not needed, so they should be left in the "normal" position.

questions.question: How can alcohol be removed from your system?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time
Safe if you eat easy foods

questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, or drinking while driving are distracting activities and should be avoided. Plan ahead and stop to eat on long trips.

questions.question: When alley docking, how should your vehicle be parked?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line
Straight within the parking space boundaries
At an angle within the parking space boundaries

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the parking space boundaries
questions.explanation: For alley docking, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley. Your vehicle must be straight within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object, you should:

options.text: Turn more than needed to have extra clearance
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object
Steer and accelerate at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object
questions.explanation: Turn only as much as necessary to clear the object. Do not apply brakes while turning.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and the car ahead is:

options.text: Not encouraged, as it slows traffic
Encouraged, as it gives you time to react to hazards
Only encouraged if you have a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged, as it gives you time to react to hazards
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires maintaining space on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to act if a problem arises.

questions.question: A modulating control valve can control the:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver gradually apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, a lever on the dashboard controls this valve.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes, which should you use?

options.text: Large vehicles should not turn where there are two left turn lanes

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need to swing right to make a left turn. When there are two left turn lanes, use the right lane to begin your turn.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS is not working while you drive, what should you do?

options.text: Use your parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: Your vehicle's basic brakes still work even if the ABS is not working. You should continue to drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: When you start the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, listen for any unusual noises. This helps you check if the engine is working properly.

questions.question: What is the maximum air loss allowed for a double combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle must not lose more than 4 psi per minute during a leakage test. Knowing the safe air loss rate for your vehicle is important.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Say nothing and hope the problem goes away.
Write a report describing the problem.
Try to fix the problem yourself.
Avoid using that part and hope others do not notice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, you may need to write a report about the vehicle. Always note any problems that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol content (BAC) is at least:
questions.explanation: Operating a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal. A first offense means you lose your license for at least one year. If you have any alcohol in your system but are below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: How much play is safe on a 20-inch steering wheel?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs required to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, no matter the size, needs a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: During the straight line backing test, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing test, you may exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Use rumble strips to slow your vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, find an escape ramp as quickly as possible. If no escape ramp exists, drive into an open field or side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, press the brake until you reach 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, what should you do to keep normal stopping power?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. The normal position is correct for all driving conditions. Always leave it set to "normal."

questions.question: What should you do when entering a foggy area?

options.text: Stop on the side of the roadway.

questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights, do not pass other vehicles, and do not stop on the roadway. The safest option is to avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: When you pull off to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What must you provide to get a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: A list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.
Your employment history for the past five years.

questions.explanation: You must submit your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check to get a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: During the driving test, when the examiner asks you to change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Always use your turn signal and only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that can damage the brakes.
To allow for a change in air pressure.
To remove bad air from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that can damage the brakes.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil. These substances can build up and damage the air brake system. Regular draining removes this buildup.

questions.question: What can happen when you overload a vehicle with cargo?

options.text: Usually nothing happens to the vehicle.
It can affect steering and brake control.
It can affect the electrical system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect steering and brake control.
questions.explanation: Overloading affects steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to recognize when cargo is overloaded or poorly balanced.

questions.question: What is true about shaded areas of the road?

options.text: They usually do not contain moisture, so they cannot freeze.
They stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler. They remain icy and slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: When driving a commercial vehicle, are you required to wear a safety belt?

options.text: No, you are not required to wear one.
Only if your vehicle does not have airbags.
Only if you are hauling more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
Yes, you must always wear one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you must always wear one.
questions.explanation: You must always wear a safety belt when driving a commercial vehicle. A safety belt is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer or more dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous. It is harder to see hazards, headlight glare affects vision, and there are more fatigued and impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: A 40-foot long item on a flatbed trailer needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: Texting while driving a CMV is:

options.text: Acceptable if the text is work-related.
Acceptable if the text has fewer than 10 words.
Encouraged because it is safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing text into or reading text from any electronic device.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Create your own route to show your driving skills.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, listen to and follow the examiner's directions. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: Driving in extremely hot weather:

options.text: Requires you to remove oil from the engine.

questions.explanation: Extremely hot weather can increase tire pressure dangerously as the air inside expands. Keep enough oil and coolant in the engine to prevent overheating.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment:

options.text: The parking brake should not be engaged.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, engage the parking brake and chock the wheels. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: When an engine starts:

options.text: The brakes should be locked up.
Warning lights come on and then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights come on and then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should go off within a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: If you have more than one license:

options.text: You are unlikely to be caught.
There is no way for authorities to find out.

questions.explanation: A person cannot have more than one license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces freeze.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful crossing bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road ahead to spot potential hazards early. Plan how to handle these hazards if they become dangerous.
